c.tagline: Sint Maarten's boardwalk capital — duty-free Front Street, Great Bay sands, and cruise-ship bustle on the Dutch side.

taxi.fareNote: No Uber or ride-hailing. Taxis use government-set fixed fares by zone (quoted per two passengers, with surcharges after 10 PM and for extra luggage); agree the price before you get in. U.S. dollars are fine.

emergency.note: On the Dutch side dial 911 for police, 912 for ambulance, and 919 for fire. The Netherlands Antillean guilder is the currency, but U.S. dollars are accepted everywhere.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Watch belongings on Front Street on busy cruise days and skip the quieter Back Street area late at night; never leave valuables on beaches or in rental cars.

hood_desc: The capital's walkable core on Great Bay — the duty-free shops of Front Street, the historic courthouse on Wathey Square, and the beachfront Boardwalk lined with open-air restaurants, casinos, and bars; the heart of the cruise-day bustle.
A resort-lined bay on the peninsula just west of town, with a calm beach, big beachfront hotels, and a golf course; an easy walk or short drive from Philipsburg yet quieter than Front Street.
A dense strip around the lagoon and yacht marina near the airport, packed with the island's best restaurants, casinos, and late-night bars; convenient and lively, popular with boaters and night owls.
The beach zone at the end of the runway, famous for Maho Beach plane-spotting, plus Mullet Bay's white sands and big resort-casinos; energetic and firmly beach-and-party focused.
A calmer, sunrise-facing stretch of the east coast, with upscale resorts, the Oyster Pond marina, and reef snorkeling off Dawn Beach; secluded and relaxed, away from the crowds.
lodging: Sonesta Maho Beach Resort Casino & Spa

water.note: Desalinated tap water is safe to drink.

transit.hours: Minibuses run mostly in daylight (around 6 AM to 7 PM); the cruise-pier water taxi runs during ship hours. Taxis fill the gaps at night.
transit.note: Sint Maarten has no rail. Visitors get around by shared minibus vans, taxis, or rental car, plus a water taxi linking the cruise pier to Philipsburg's Boardwalk. The island is small, so cross-border trips to the French side take under 30 minutes.
transit.pay: Shared minibus vans charge about $1-2 (or the guilder equivalent), paid in cash to the driver — wave one down along the road. The cruise-pier water taxi to the Boardwalk runs on a paid day-pass. Taxis use fixed government-set fares.

bus: Public minibuses (shared vans) to Simpson Bay, Marigot, and across the island
ferry: Water taxi from the cruise pier to the Boardwalk / Great Bay
Ferries to Saba and St. Eustatius (Statia)

transit.m: Taxi from SXM to Philipsburg (15-20 min)
Public minibus toward Philipsburg via Simpson Bay (infrequent)

tip.r: Many restaurants add a 10-15% service charge; if not, 15-18% is customary. U.S. dollars are accepted everywhere alongside the guilder.

landmarks: Great Bay Boardwalk
Philipsburg's palm-lined seafront promenade, curving along Great Bay Beach past pastel cafés, with cruise ships and green hills completing the postcard.
Front Street (Voorstraat)
The capital's famous duty-free artery, where jewelry emporiums and rum shops occupy gingerbread-trimmed Caribbean townhouses a shell's throw from the beach.
The Courthouse
Sint Maarten's beloved 1793 white-and-green landmark topped with a pineapple finial, still working as a courthouse at the head of Front Street.
Fort Amsterdam
The Dutch Caribbean's first fort, raised in 1631 on a peninsula between bays, now a ruin patrolled by brown pelicans with superb harbor views.
Sint Maarten Museum
A charming Front Street museum tracing Arawak artifacts, salt-industry history and Hurricane Luis relics, including treasures from the 1801 HMS Proselyte wreck.
Maho Beach
The world-famous strip of sand at the runway's end where jumbo jets skim sunbathers' heads, an unforgettable short hop from Philipsburg.
Great Salt Pond
The vast lagoon behind town that birthed Sint Maarten's salt economy, today a birdwatching haven and stage for Carnival village festivities.
Rainforest Adventures Rockland Estate
A hillside eco-park on a historic sugar estate, launching the world's steepest zipline, the Flying Dutchman, from Sentry Hill's panoramic summit.
Little Bay Beach
A tranquil golden cove beneath Fort Amsterdam's headland, prized for calm snorkeling water and views across to distant Saba.
Old Street
A quaint pedestrian lane off Front Street, its brightly painted colonial facades, arcades and boutiques making it Philipsburg's most photogenic shopping detour.

train.note: There is no railway on Sint Maarten or anywhere in the Leeward Islands. Arrive by air into Princess Juliana International Airport - famous for the low approach over Maho Beach - or by cruise ship, or by ferry from neighbouring islands.

intl.to: Marigot & Grand Case (Saint-Martin, France) - across the open island border
intl.op: local minibus operators — pay the driver

bus.note: The island is split between Dutch and French halves with an open border and no formalities, so the minibuses that run between Philipsburg and Marigot cross what is technically an international frontier without stopping. Fares are a couple of dollars, paid to the driver, and buses run frequently through the day but thin out in the evening.

intl.to: Anguilla - Blowing Point (UK) - from Marigot or the Simpson Bay ferry terminal, ~25 min

ferry.note: Sint Maarten is the ferry hub of the northern Leewards, with genuine international crossings to Anguilla and St Barth several times a day. The Anguilla boats mostly leave from Blowing Point on the French side at Marigot, while the St Barth fast ferries run from Philipsburg's Bobby's Marina and Simpson Bay. Bring your passport, and note that crossings get bumpy in winter swell.

half.name: Marigot
half.blurb: French-side capital of the same island, about 20 minutes by road, holds a hilltop fort, an outdoor market and beachfront restaurants.

half.name: The Valley
half.blurb: Anguilla's low-key capital, reached by a short ferry from Marigot, sits near Shoal Bay's turquoise water and coral-sand beaches.

half.name: Gustavia
half.blurb: St. Barts' harbor town, about 90 minutes by ferry, is lined with yacht-filled marinas, French boutiques and hillside villas.

half.name: Windwardside
half.blurb: Village on the volcanic island of Saba, a short flight away, sits along hiking trails up Mount Scenery amid steep, terraced hillsides.
